current_route_overlap.inputs: Bid.path tuples for the two selected tasks
current_route_overlap.geometry: Each bid carries only an ordered bounded XY sample polyline in shared_map; generator paths are sampled to at most 16 points and LocalNav2 paths to at most 32 points.
current_route_overlap.sampling_interval: No fixed spatial interval. Downsampling is index-spaced; candidate-generator samples at most 16 evenly by pose index, LocalNav2 at most 32 evenly by pose index.
current_route_overlap.threshold: 2*route_corridor_radius_m = 0.32 m point-to-point threshold with default radius 0.16 m.
current_route_overlap.directionality: Unsigned symmetric average of two one-way sample-match fractions.
current_route_overlap.distinguishes_crossing: No; a single crossing and a long shared corridor both become a scalar fraction, with some dependence on sample density.
current_route_overlap.where_along_path: No; only one scalar is returned and matched indices/intervals are discarded.
current_route_overlap.geometry_output: No overlap geometry, intervals or conflict-zone endpoints.
current_route_overlap.time_or_eta: None. Bid has a path-query timestamp, but route_overlap does not use it and no path speed/time parameter is transported.
current_route_overlap.costmap_width: No costmap input; route_overlap cannot determine whether a shared section is too narrow for two footprints to pass.

available_reusable_data.peer_bids: Both peers retain current-round bid batches, including selected-task path samples, while the round is active/navigating.
available_reusable_data.path_frame: The task/bid wire messages do not carry a path frame field; current code and publishers use shared_map by convention.
available_reusable_data.current_pose: The allocator has its own odometry and TF for LocalNav2 health, but it does not publish or consume peer pose in the protocol.
available_reusable_data.costmaps: LocalNav2 subscribes to each namespace's global_costmap/costmap for dispatch checks; no shared costmap or common obstacle-width computation is exposed by the allocator.
available_reusable_data.collision_monitor: Production Nav2 launches include Collision Monitor with a 0.08 m stop circle and lidar input, which is reactive contact prevention, not a reservation/deadlock scheduler.

can_refactor_to_detect_conflict_zone.answer: Partially, without changing Nav2: existing sampled paths are enough to identify contiguous sample-index runs that are geometrically close.
required_new_work: retain matched sample indices and convert them to path-distance intervals
define a shared conflict-zone threshold using robot footprint plus clearance rather than the current 0.32 m soft corridor threshold
obtain a common costmap/occupancy geometry and determine traversable width
add fresh robot poses and a deterministic ETA model
add a reservation/occupancy/release message or a rigorously shared TF-based state machine
can_refactor_to_detect_conflict_zone.nav2_change: Not intrinsically required; the safest first implementation gates dispatch or holds before Nav2 starts rather than injecting velocity commands.

proposed_scheduler_feasibility.peer_pose_frequency: Not available in current allocator messages. Global TF may contain both robot frames in this project, but the assignment node has no peer-pose query, freshness policy or wire agreement for it.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.both_paths_at_both_peers: Yes for the current round, as bounded Bid.path samples; not full nav_msgs/Path geometry.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.same_conflict_zone_independently: A sampled-path proximity interval could be deterministic from the common round bids. A true narrow-zone test cannot be guaranteed because local costmaps and footprint/clearance data are not currently part of the agreement.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.deterministic_eta: Not currently. Path length is available, but start pose, speed model and current time are not protocol-bound. A fixed configured speed plus common TF could be deterministic after a new freshness rule.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.safe_hold_point: No existing helper. It would need a path prefix before the conflict interval, map/costmap free-space and footprint-clearance validation, and a fallback to not dispatch if no safe hold point exists.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.pause_without_cancel: No. LocalNav2 exposes send/cancel only; the allocator deliberately has no cmd_vel publisher. Zero-command gating could trip Nav2 progress checks and Collision Monitor is not a pause/reservation API.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.delay_dispatch: Yes, cleaner and safer: leave the agreed task/decision intact, gate the lower-priority peer before send_navigation, and release only from an explicit winner-clear condition.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.conflict_emerges_after_dispatch: Do not cancel or inject a stop from this layer for the first implementation. Keep Nav2/Collision Monitor reactive safety and handle only pre-dispatch conflicts; a later version needs a reservation state machine for already-active goals.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.minimum_tomorrow_demo: Add a pre-dispatch deterministic gate for already-known conflicting sampled-path intervals, with one reservation owner, a lower-priority not-yet-dispatched state, a safe current-pose hold, and a release heartbeat. If the necessary common pose/clearance evidence is absent, conservatively serialize the two conflicting dispatches rather than guess a hold point.
proposed_scheduler_feasibility.robot_id_priority: Robot ID should remain only the final tie-break after occupied-zone status and ETA; the current architecture does not yet provide the primary occupied/ETA facts.
